title: Deep-Dish Thyme Chicken Pie with Double Crust
dek: Large, juicy chicken pieces and a thyme-scented savory gravy tucked between two deeply golden, flaky pastry crusts.
image_alt: Thick slice of double-crust chicken pie showing large chicken pieces beneath a deeply golden flaky pastry top
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
3/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
1 1/2 tsp fresh thyme leaves, plus more for serving

instructions.name: Heat the oven and line the dish
instructions.text: Set a rack in the lower third of the oven and heat to 400°F. Fit one cold crust into a deep 9-inch pie plate, leaving the overhang in place. Refrigerate the lined plate while you make the filling.

instructions.name: Brown the chicken in two batches
instructions.text: Pat the chicken dry and season with 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high. Brown half the chicken for about 3 minutes, turning once; transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining oil and chicken. The centers may still be underdone.

instructions.name: Build the savory gravy
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add onion and celery and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add butter. When melted, sprinkle in flour and stir constantly for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in broth, then milk. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.

instructions.name: Finish and cool the filling
instructions.text: Stir in Dijon, thyme, nutmeg, the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Return the chicken and accumulated juices. Simmer for 2 minutes, then spread the filling on a rimmed plate and cool for 15 minutes; hot filling can melt the bottom crust before it starts to set.

instructions.name: Seal the double crust
instructions.text: Spoon the warm—not steaming—filling into the lined pie plate. Lay the second crust over the top. Trim to a 1/2-inch overhang, fold both crust edges under together, and crimp firmly. Cut four 1-inch vents in the center. Beat the egg with 1 tablespoon water and brush a thin coat over the pastry.

instructions.name: Bake until deeply golden and safe
instructions.text: Place the pie on a rimmed pan and bake at 400°F for 45 to 50 minutes, rotating once, until the crust is deeply golden and the filling bubbles through the vents. Insert an instant-read thermometer through a vent into a chicken piece; it must reach 165°F. Shield the edge with foil if it darkens too quickly.

instructions.name: Rest before slicing
instructions.text: Cool the pie on a rack for 20 minutes. This pause lets the gravy thicken enough to hold the large chicken pieces in a clean slice. Finish with a few fresh thyme leaves and serve warm.

why_it_works: Briefly browning large chicken pieces develops savory flavor while leaving enough cooking time for them to finish gently inside the pie.
Cooling the thickened filling before assembly protects the bottom crust from melting into the gravy.
A lower-third oven rack directs more heat toward the bottom crust, while the egg wash helps the top brown evenly.
swaps: Use 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs and verify they reach at least 165°F; their richer meat is especially forgiving.
Replace celery with 1 cup finely diced leek, rinsed very well, for a sweeter allium flavor.
For a dairy-free filling, use unsweetened oat milk and plant-based butter; check the pie crust label because some refrigerated crusts contain dairy.
storage: Refrigerate cooled pie, tightly covered, for up to 4 days. Reheat individual slices on a pan at 350°F for 18 to 22 minutes until the center reaches 165°F; the oven restores the crust better than a microwave. Freeze fully cooled slices for up to 2 months, thaw overnight, and reheat the same way.
notes: Use a true deep-dish 9-inch pie plate; a standard shallow plate can overflow.
Keep both crusts cold until assembly. If the top crust feels soft after crimping, chill the assembled pie for 10 minutes before baking.
Set the pie plate on a rimmed pan before baking to catch any butter or gravy that escapes.

faqs.q: Can I assemble the chicken pie ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Prepare and cool the filling up to 2 days ahead. For the crispest bottom crust, keep it separate and assemble the pie just before baking. A fully assembled unbaked pie can be refrigerated for up to 4 hours.

faqs.q: Why did my bottom crust turn soggy?
faqs.a: The usual causes are hot filling, gravy that was not simmered until thick, or cutting immediately after baking. Cool the filling, use the lower oven rack, and give the finished pie the full 20-minute rest.
Use 4 cups of large pulled pieces and skip the browning step. Add the cooked chicken only after the gravy thickens, then proceed; the assembled filling still needs to reach 165°F in the oven.

title: Warm Butternut Quinoa Salad with Feta & Cranberries
dek: Caramelized squash and mushrooms, fluffy quinoa, tangy feta, tart cranberries, and tender greens tossed in maple-Dijon dressing.
image_alt: Warm quinoa salad with butternut squash, browned mushrooms, dried cranberries, feta chunks, and tender green leaves
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups dry quinoa, rinsed in a fine-mesh sieve
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
4 cups peeled butternut squash cut into 3/4-inch cubes (about 1 1/2 lb)
6 oz feta cheese, broken into bite-size chunks

instructions.name: Cook the quinoa
instructions.text: Combine rinsed quinoa, water, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

instructions.name: Season the vegetables
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. On a large rimmed pan, toss squash and mushrooms with 2 tablespoons olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, black pepper, and a generous pinch of salt. Spread everything in one uncrowded layer.

instructions.name: Caramelize the squash and mushrooms
instructions.text: Cook for 24 to 28 minutes, turning once after 15 minutes, until the squash is tender through the center and browned at the edges and the mushrooms have released their moisture. The largest squash cube should crush easily with a fork.

instructions.name: Whisk the maple-Dijon dressing
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, whisk apple cider vinegar, Dijon, maple syrup, garlic, the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, and 1 tablespoon warm water until emulsified. Taste and add salt a pinch at a time; the feta will add more seasoning.

instructions.name: Dress while warm
instructions.text: Add warm quinoa, hot squash and mushrooms, dried cranberries, and parsley to the dressing. Toss thoroughly so the quinoa absorbs the dressing and the cranberries begin to soften.

instructions.name: Fold in the delicate ingredients
instructions.text: Let the quinoa mixture stand for 5 minutes so it is warm rather than piping hot. Fold in the spring greens and two-thirds of the feta just until the leaves soften slightly. Spoon into bowls and scatter the remaining feta over the top.

why_it_works: Rinsing quinoa removes its naturally bitter outer coating, while a covered five-minute rest keeps the grains separate and fluffy.
High heat and an uncrowded pan brown the squash and mushrooms instead of steaming them.
Tossing the sturdy components with dressing while warm helps the quinoa absorb flavor; adding greens and feta later protects their texture.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato cubes in place of butternut squash; begin checking them after 22 minutes.
Replace feta with goat cheese, or use a firm plant-based feta for a dairy-free salad.
Substitute chopped dried cherries or golden raisins for cranberries, adjusting maple syrup down to 1 teaspoon if the fruit is very sweet.
storage: Refrigerate the dressed quinoa, vegetables, cranberries, and feta in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Store fresh greens separately when meal-prepping. Eat chilled or rewarm the quinoa mixture for 60 to 90 seconds in the microwave until just warm, then add the greens. Do not freeze; the greens and feta lose their texture.
notes: Pre-cut squash saves time, but cut any oversized pieces down to 3/4 inch so they finish together.
A fine-mesh sieve is essential for rinsing quinoa without losing the tiny grains.
For meal prep, divide the greens among containers only after the warm quinoa mixture has cooled completely.

faqs.q: Is this salad filling enough for dinner?
faqs.a: Yes. Quinoa, feta, squash, and mushrooms make it substantial. Each serving is about 374 calories; for a larger appetite, add a drained can of chickpeas and increase the dressing vinegar by 1 tablespoon.

Yes. Chill the dressed quinoa and vegetables, then fold in the greens and feta immediately before serving. Let it sit at room temperature for 10 minutes so the dressing is not muted by refrigerator cold.
Too much water or skipping the covered rest can make quinoa wet. Measure 2 3/4 cups water precisely, keep the simmer low, and fluff only after the five-minute off-heat rest.

title: Blackberry-Blueberry Cornmeal Cobbler with Crisp Sugar Crust
dek: Jammy blackberries and blueberries bubble through a golden cornmeal topping finished with a delicate, crunchy sugar crust.
image_alt: Blackberry and blueberry cornmeal cobbler in a white rectangular baking dish with a crisp golden sugar crust
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen blackberries (about 20 oz)
2 cups fresh or frozen blueberries (about 10 oz)
6 tbsp cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
3/4 cup whole buttermilk, plus 1 tbsp if needed
Vanilla ice cream or softly whipped cream, for serving (optional)

instructions.name: Heat the oven and prepare the dish
instructions.text: Set a rack in the center of the oven and heat to 375°F. Lightly butter a 9-by-13-inch ceramic or glass baking dish and set it on a rimmed pan to catch any bubbling fruit.

instructions.name: Season the berries
instructions.text: In the baking dish, gently toss blackberries and blueberries with 1/3 cup granulated sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, lemon zest, and vanilla until no dry starch remains. Spread the fruit evenly and let it stand while you make the topping.

instructions.name: Cut the butter into the dry ingredients
instructions.text: Whisk flour, cornmeal, baking powder, salt, and the remaining 1/3 cup granulated sugar in a medium bowl. Add cold butter and work it in with your fingertips or a pastry blender until the largest pieces are pea-size.

instructions.name: Mix a tender cornmeal dough
instructions.text: Pour in 3/4 cup buttermilk and fold just until no dry flour remains. If crumbly pockets persist, add the extra tablespoon buttermilk. Do not knead; a rough, moist dough makes a tender topping.

instructions.name: Top without sealing the fruit
instructions.text: Drop the dough over the berries in 12 rough mounds, leaving small gaps for steam and juices to escape. Sprinkle the turbinado sugar evenly over the dough.

instructions.name: Bake until bubbling and crisp
instructions.text: Bake at 375°F for 42 to 48 minutes, rotating after 25 minutes, until berry juices bubble vigorously in the center and the cornmeal topping is deep golden. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a topping mound should register about 200°F.

instructions.name: Cool to thicken the juices
instructions.text: Cool on a rack for at least 25 minutes before spooning into bowls. The filling thickens as it drops from oven-hot to warm. Serve with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream if desired.

why_it_works: Cornstarch thickens the berry juices only after they reach a full bubble, so checking the center prevents a runny cobbler.
Fine cornmeal adds toasted flavor and a delicate crunch without making the topping gritty.
Cold butter and minimal mixing leave small fat pockets that create a tender, craggy topping beneath the crisp sugar finish.
swaps: Use 6 cups blueberries or 6 cups blackberries instead of the blend; keep the cornstarch amount the same.
No buttermilk? Stir 2 teaspoons lemon juice into 3/4 cup whole milk and let it stand for 5 minutes.
For a less-sweet cobbler, reduce the sugar mixed with the berries to 1/4 cup, but keep the topping sugar unchanged for structure and browning.
storage: Cover and refrigerate cooled cobbler for up to 4 days. Reheat uncovered at 325°F for 15 to 20 minutes until warm, or microwave individual portions for 30 to 45 seconds. For best texture, freeze portions in airtight containers for up to 2 months, thaw overnight, then use the oven method.
notes: Frozen berries can go into the dish without thawing; expect the cobbler to need 5 to 8 extra minutes.
Use fine or medium cornmeal, not coarse polenta, which stays gritty in the short baking time.
The rimmed pan is insurance against fruit syrup bubbling over the sides of the baking dish.

faqs.q: How do I know the cobbler is done in the middle?
faqs.a: Look for active bubbles through the center gaps, not only around the rim. The topping should be deep golden and about 200°F inside; pale dough or a cool center needs more time.

faqs.q: Can I make this cobbler ahead?
faqs.a: Mix the dry topping ingredients and prepare the berry mixture up to 8 hours ahead, but refrigerate them separately. Cut in the butter, add buttermilk, and assemble just before baking so the leavener stays active.

faqs.q: Why is my berry filling thin?
faqs.a: Cornstarch needs a full simmer to thicken. If the center never bubbled, return the cobbler to the oven for 5 to 10 minutes. Also allow the 25-minute cooling time before serving.
